about: What is known of each SOLIDWORKS API member (entry U1.1). Read by api_signature and api_search; checked by the contracts: every member must exist in the interop, every enum map must name a real parameter and a real swconst enum, measured types only on parameters declared Object, indices only on "return" or a real parameter. A member that is not here is never_probed. Enum maps and index meanings are written only when known: anything else is "enum not tabulated" / "index not tabulated".

states.forbidden: never called by the bridge (crash, modal, arbitrary code, the whole application)
states.confirm: writes to disk or does what cannot be undone: asks a person first
states.gray: called and measured to lie, return nothing usable or behave only sometimes
states.probed_read: called and measured: reads, does not modify
states.probed_modifies: called and measured: modifies the model

IAssemblyDoc.AddMate5.why: 15 arguments, mostly Double/Int32/Boolean positional -- a position mistake mates silently, no exception. Measured 2026-09-17: no special "selection mark" is needed (that unknown, once rated 8-10h, turned out to not exist): plain IEntity.Select4(append:true, null) on the two entities, then AddMate5, answers swAddMateError_NoError. IMPORTANT: in swAddMateError_e, NoError = 1 and ErrorUnknown = 0 -- a naive 'if (errore != 0)' would report a successful mate as failed. swMateAlign_e has three pairs of names on the same value: swAlignNONE = swMateAlignALIGNED = 0, swAlignSAME = swMateAlignANTI_ALIGNED = 1, swAlignAGAINST = swMateAlignCLOSEST = 2. "SAME" is worth "ANTI_ALIGNED": same number, opposite sense. The bridge writes swMateAlignANTI_ALIGNED / swMateAlignALIGNED (OperazioniAccoppia.cs:109).

IAssemblyDoc.CreateMateData.why: The Type parameter is declared Int32 and which enum it takes is NOT tabulated: reflection cannot say it, and nobody has measured it yet. Entry U11.3 measures it; until then api_signature says "enum not tabulated".

IModelDocExtension.IsSamePersistentID.why: Returns Int32, NOT Boolean: it is a swObjectEquality (swObjectNotSame = 0, swObjectSame = 1, swObjectUnsupported = 2). The "true 46 times out of 46" of Z-A7 does not say which of the two non-zero values it was. The decision not to use it does not change: if it was 1 it never discriminated, if it was 2 it is not supported. GetObjectByPersistReference3 + a corroborating read are used instead.

IMathTransform.ArrayData.why: 16 numbers. Measured layout: indices 0-8 are the 3x3 rotation matrix stored ROW-MAJOR (row i = indices 3i, 3i+1, 3i+2); indices 9-11 are the translation; index 12 onward: index not tabulated. IMPORTANT: the plane-normal use case measured that the normal is the THIRD ROW (indices 6,7,8), not the third column -- on two of three test planes row and column gave the same answer (50/50 chance of picking the wrong one forever), the third (oblique) plane exposed the difference: row gives the correct (0,-.7071,.7071), column gives the wrong (0,.7071,.7071). Separately, on IComponent2.GetTotalTransform, indices 9-11 were confirmed as translation by asking for z=30 and reading back [0,-2,30] (see IAssemblyDoc.AddComponent5 for the -2 explanation) and predicting+confirming a second case at (0,-5,0).

return.0-8: 3x3 rotation, row-major (row i = 3i..3i+2); a plane normal is the THIRD ROW 6-8 (measured on an oblique plane, 16/9/2026)
return.9-11: translation, metres (measured on IComponent2.GetTotalTransform: z = 30 mm read back as [0, -2, 30] mm)

IBody2.GetMassProperties.why: Returns a double[] (declared Object). MEASURED index 3 = volume in cubic meters: on 2026-09-09, eleven guided-hole sizes M3 through M24 all matched pi*r^2*depth at the tenth of a cubic millimeter using index 3. IMPORTANT: a member named IBody2.GetVolume does NOT exist in the inventory -- it is one of several names that 'sounded right' and were not; GetMassProperties(density) is the real member. GetBodies2 (needed to get the IBody2 instances) lives on IPartDoc, not on IModelDoc2.

return.3: volume, cubic metres (measured 9/9/2026 on eleven guided holes M3-M24)
return.0-2: centre of mass, metres (used by green bench cases: volume-weighted centre of several bodies)

ICurve.CircleParams.why: Returns a double[] (declared Object). The slots below are the ones the code reads and green bench cases check (thread diameter = [6] x 2000 mm, centre marks, hole callouts); the other slots are not tabulated.

IModelDoc2.EditDelete.why: Forbidden by contract (ProveLeFirmeVietate). Measured still alive in the codebase on 2026-09-27: OperazioniTabellaFori.cs:358 called modello.EditDelete() to remove a wrongly-created hole table; must be replaced with IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2 as already done in OperazioniSw.cs:5852.

IModelDocExtension.AddDimension.why: Measured 2026-09-11: opens the "Modifica" modal dialog and the COM call never returns while swInputDimValOnCreate is on. Also measured to return null in every sketch-point+model-edge combination tried, and for point-to-point (arc centers) dimensions, and for two silhouette entities. This is exactly the AddDimension the U1.4 forbidden list names.

IFeatureManager.FeatureExtrusion3.why: 23 positional arguments. The end conditions T1/T2 are swEndConditions_e and the start condition T0 is swStartConditions_e (the code passes them by enum name). The U1 acceptance plate (100x60x10 = 60,000 mm3) is built with it.

IFeatureManager.InsertWeldmentTrimFeatur.why: MEASURED 2026-09-25 on a two-member weldment frame (taglia_membri): with object[] for BodiesToTrim/BodiesOrFaces the interop marshals a VARIANT array and SOLIDWORKS answers with a feature that never enters the tree -- part unchanged, NO error at all. With Body2[] typed arrays (or DispatchWrapper[]) the cut is real: volume drops by the expected -58798.23 mm3. This is the cardinal defense of the whole bridge (U1.3): arguments must always be converted to the type the signature declares.

measured_types.BodiesToTrim: Body2[] (DispatchWrapper[] also works; object[] makes a phantom feature)
measured_types.BodiesOrFaces: Body2[] or Face2[] (DispatchWrapper[] also works; object[] makes a phantom feature)
